title: Scheme ampleness characterized by the canonical section-algebra Proj map
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Say $L$ is $f$-ample if its restriction to $f^{-1}(V)$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $V\subseteq T$. If $L$ is $f$-ample, then $f$ is quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $f$ is quasi-compact and separated, form the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes d}$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], the relative Proj $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj], and the evaluation homomorphism $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$, where $f^*$ is [def-pc-module-pullback] and $f_*N(V)=N(f^{-1}(V))$. Let $U(\psi)$ and $r_{L,\psi}$ denote the generation locus and canonical map of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map], interpreted on schemes. Then $L$ is $f$-ample if and only if $U(\psi)=X$ and $r_{L,\psi}:X\to P$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].
